newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Weather - Light rain, crop prospects same.
newsitem.headline: Australian Weather - Light rain, crop prospects same.

text.p: Scattered rain in Australia over the past week has done little to improve crop prospects in parched eastern states and in the country's south, weather officials and grains industry sources said on Monday.

Rainfall over the past week in the main eastern wheat-producing state of New South Wales (NSW) was mostly confined to the coast, although widespread falls occurred across the state on July 27 and 28, a weather official said.
Heavy falls of rain, however, were concentrated in the south of the state in the Thredbo snowfields area, he said.
In Victoria, falls of five to 10 millimetres occurred last weekend in scattered areas, but widespread substantial rainfall did not take place, another state weather official said.
Falls in the most important of the state's wheat-growing areas were only about one millimetre, he said.
Rainfall in the past week in South Australia also did not amount to anything substantial enough to raise crop prospects, an official with this state's weather bureau told Reuters.
Canberra-based officials with government departments which cover Australian primary industries said on Monday that rainfall patterns had not changed in the past week to alter crop prospects.
Crop prospects in Western Australia, which falls outside the El Nino drought impact which is concentrated on Australia's east side, remain the best in the country, wheat industry officials say.
Western Australia's production for the current season appears headed for the seven million mark, against 7.7 million tonnes last season, grains industry officials said.
However, NSW appears headed for a crop of only about four million tonnes against 8.6 million tonnes last year.
South Australia and Victoria are all presently headed for crops of 1.2-1.4 million tonnes, against 2.8 million tonnes and 2.4 million tonnes last season respectively, they said.
Queensland's production presently appears headed for 1.4 million tonnes, against 1.9 million tonnes last season.
Australia's total wheat crop now appears likely to be less than 15 million tonnes, against record production of 23.5 million tonnes in 1996/97, industry executives say.
This is down from a recently revised forecast of 15 to 16 million tonnes by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB).
The AWB is expected to announce a revised crop forecast with its latest pool price update, later on Monday.
